# jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app (Data Source)

Looks up an app's App Store listing, so a `jamfplatform_pro_mac_app_store_app` or `jamfplatform_pro_mobile_device_app` can take its name, version, bundle identifier, store URL, description and icon from the App Store, and you do not copy them by hand. Set exactly one of `id`, `bundle_id` or `store_url`, and set `target` to the kind of app record the values feed.

The listing is read again on every plan. When the developer releases a new version, `version` changes and an app record that uses it shows the new version as a planned change. Pin `general.version` or list it in `lifecycle.ignore_changes` to keep releases out of plans.

The icon follows the listing the same way. When the developer changes the app's artwork, `icon_url` changes, the next plan replaces the `jamfplatform_pro_icon` built from it, and the app record picks up the new icon. Expect that replacement after any artwork change.

The App Store does not list custom apps distributed to a single organization, so you cannot look one up. The lookup reads the App Store directly and needs no Jamf Pro permission.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Mac: look up Pages by its App Store ID. A Mac target reads the Mac listing,
# which has its own icon, description and version.
data "jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app" "pages_mac" {
  id     = "361309726"
  target = "mac"
}

# The provider downloads the icon from the App Store. When the developer changes
# the artwork, icon_url changes and the next plan replaces this icon.
resource "jamfplatform_pro_icon" "pages_mac" {
  icon_file_source = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.icon_url
}

resource "jamfplatform_pro_mac_app_store_app" "pages" {
  general = {
    name            = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.name
    version         = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.version
    bundle_id       = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.bundle_id
    url             = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.url
    is_free         = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.is_free
    deployment_type = "Make Available in Self Service"
  }

  self_service = {
    self_service_description = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.pages_mac.description
    self_service_icon = {
      id = jamfplatform_pro_icon.pages_mac.id
    }
  }

  # Each App Store release changes version. Ignore it here to keep releases out
  # of plans, or leave it managed to record every release as a planned change.
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [general.version]
  }
}

# Mobile device: look up Keynote by bundle ID in the UK App Store.
data "jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app" "keynote_mobile" {
  bundle_id      = "com.apple.Keynote"
  target         = "mobile_device"
  country_region = "GB"
}

resource "jamfplatform_pro_icon" "keynote_mobile" {
  icon_file_source = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.icon_url
}

resource "jamfplatform_pro_mobile_device_app" "keynote" {
  general = {
    name                  = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.name
    version               = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.version
    bundle_id             = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.bundle_id
    itunes_store_url      = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.url
    itunes_country_region = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.country_region
    is_free               = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.is_free
  }

  self_service = {
    self_service_description = data.jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app.keynote_mobile.description
    self_service_icon = {
      id = jamfplatform_pro_icon.keynote_mobile.id
    }
  }

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [general.version]
  }
}

# You can also look up an app by its store link. The provider uses the link's
# country or region when country_region is not set.
data "jamfplatform_apple_app_store_app" "from_link" {
  store_url = "https://apps.apple.com/us/app/xcode/id497799835?mt=12"
  target    = "mac"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `target` (String) The kind of app record the values feed: `mac` for `jamfplatform_pro_mac_app_store_app` (Mac Apps) or `mobile_device` for `jamfplatform_pro_mobile_device_app` (Mobile Device Apps). An app sold for both has a separate Mac listing with its own icon, description and version, so the target must match the record. Looking up an iPhone and iPad app with `mac` finds nothing. One of `mac`, `mobile_device`.

### Optional

- `bundle_id` (String) App bundle identifier, such as `com.apple.dt.Xcode`. Set exactly one of `id`, `bundle_id` or `store_url`. Jamf Pro stores a bundle identifier exactly as written, so the provider rejects a value whose letter case differs from the App Store listing and names the listed spelling. When you look up by `id` or `store_url`, the provider fills this in from the listing. Use it for `general.bundle_id`.
- `country_region` (String) Two-letter App Store country or region code in upper case, such as `US` or `GB`. Defaults to the one in `store_url`, then `US`. The App Store answers a code it does not recognise from the US App Store, so the provider rejects one. Use it for `general.itunes_country_region` on a mobile device app.
- `id` (String) App Store ID: the number after `id` in the app's App Store link (`497799835` for Xcode). Set exactly one of `id`, `bundle_id` or `store_url`. When you look up by `bundle_id` or `store_url`, the provider fills this in from the listing.
- `language` (String) Language for the listing's name and description, such as `en` or `fr`. When the country or region does not offer it, the App Store answers in that country's default language.
- `store_url` (String) The app's App Store link, such as `https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/pages-create-documents/id361309726`. Set exactly one of `id`, `bundle_id` or `store_url`. When `country_region` is not set, the provider uses the link's country or region.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) App description as listed, without trailing whitespace, which Jamf Pro drops when it saves a description. Use it for `self_service.self_service_description`.
- `genres` (List of String) App Store categories, primary category first.
- `icon_url` (String) URL of the app's icon as a 512 × 512 PNG. Use it as `icon_file_source` on a `jamfplatform_pro_icon`, and set the app record's `self_service.self_service_icon.id` to that icon. Null when the listing has no icon.
- `is_free` (Boolean) Whether the app is free in `country_region`. Use it for `general.is_free`.
- `name` (String) App name as listed. Use it for `general.name`.
- `url` (String) App Store URL of the listing in `country_region`. Use it for `general.url` on a Mac app or `general.itunes_store_url` on a mobile device app.
- `version` (String) Version currently on sale. Use it for `general.version`.
- `vpp_device_based_licensing` (Boolean) Whether licenses bought through Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager can be assigned to devices rather than to users. The app record's `vpp.assign_vpp_device_based_licenses = true` depends on it.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
